reconstructed_theorem_text: Let (Omega,m,mu) be a finite measure space with filtration F, T>0, scalar Brownian motion B with F, and the usual conditions. Here scalar Brownian motion with filtration means centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), mu-almost surely continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and independence of B(t)-B(s) from F_s for every s<=t. Zero at time zero is part of the scalar law almost surely. Usual conditions mean that every mu-null subset of Omega is in every F_t, and F is right-continuous. A progressive L2 integrand is a real process strongly progressive for F and in L2(mu product lambda_T), where lambda_T is Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T], transported to NNReal. I_eta denotes its specified continuous completed Ito integral against the given scalar Brownian driver: the canonical limit of elementary integrals, set to zero on its exceptional null set, and held constant after T. Fix a progressive L2 integrand eta on [0,T], deterministic nonnegative times s<=t<=T, and an event E belonging to F_s. There exists a progressive L2 integrand theta on [0,T] such that, pointwise for every r>=0 and omega, theta(r,omega)=1_E(omega)*1_{s<r<=t}*eta(r,omega). Moreover, for every deterministic u<=T, I_theta(u,omega)=1_E(omega)*(I_eta(min(t,u),omega)-I_eta(min(s,u),omega)) for mu-almost every omega. The exceptional set in this last equality may depend on u.
objects: Finite measure space, F,T,B, eta, interval endpoints s,t, F_s-event E, existential theta, completed integrals.
domains: Time NNReal; eta and theta real progressive L2 processes on mu product lambda_T; E a subset of Omega measurable in F_s.
quantifiers: For every admissible data, exists one theta with a process formula for all r and omega, and for all u<=T an a.e. integral identity.
assumptions: mu finite; T>0; scalar Brownian with F; usual conditions; eta progressive L2; s<=t<=T; E in F_s.
conclusion: Existence of the event-and-interval-truncated integrand, with its indicated pointwise body and prefix Ito identity.
scopes: Theta formula for all nonnegative r and all omega; stochastic identity for each u in [0,T] only a.e. (forall u then a.e. omega); s=t allowed.
constant_dependencies: Theta can depend on eta,E,s,t,F,mu,T; Ito processes additionally depend on B. No numerical bound asserted.
